problem: Collisions are normally avoided, and a single collision gives little information about scene geometry. Prior work (e.g. Learning to Fly by Crashing) uses collisions only for a binary crash-within-k-steps signal and does not recover scene geometry or predict for remote points.
motivation: Bumps are cheap, sensor-light supervision that needs no depth, maps or human labels, and works with non-geometric modalities such as sound. A single time-to-collision is a noisy overestimate, but the full distribution over collision times, conditioned on heading, encodes the shortest plausible distance and the scene layout.
key_idea: Collision replay: unwind a random walk from each collision to label earlier observations with steps-to-collision, then learn a heading-conditioned categorical distribution over collision times from images or sound, and decode it into a distance function or floorplan.
insight: Classifying the full distribution beats regression because regression targets the mean or median, which systematically over-estimates the distance to the nearest obstacle (regression over-predicts in 90% of cases vs 60% for classification). Gambler's-ruin analysis shows near-shortest paths are reasonably common in random walks, so the low quantile of the distribution recovers the true distance. Heading conditioning helps (MAE 0.16 to 0.11 in Table 1), and the distributions capture semantic space categories (AUROC 0.72).
method: Collision replay labeling: along a random-walk trajectory, the step where the collision occurs is labeled 0 steps, the previous step 1, and so on. For remote points, the location at step j is projected into the image at an earlier step i with label k-j, using intended egomotion, so it also gives labels through occlusion.
Heading-conditioned distribution model: a multinomial over 11 classes (0..9 and 10+ steps), trained with cross-entropy, taking image features, projected depth and a sin/cos heading angle.
PIFu-style remote predictor: ImageNet ResNet-18 with FPN, features bilinearly sampled at the projected query point (1024-d) and concatenated with depth and heading, then an MLP (1024-512-256).

Egocentric predictor: ResNet-18 (or an Audio-CNN for binaural spectrograms) plus an MLP that outputs 11x3 logits, one distribution per next action (left, forward, right). Inputs are 32x32 RGB or echolocation spectrograms from SoundSpaces.

Distance function decoding: the first step where cumulative probability exceeds epsilon, with linear interpolation between bins, then a min over 32 headings (or over actions in the egocentric case). Thresholding gives a floorplan.

Random-walk data with actuation noise: 10 walks of 500 steps in each of 360 Gibson scenes, using the Active Neural SLAM noise model. Frames are filtered to 800K images and the agent turns around after a collision.
Distribution similarity analysis: heading-aligned Jensen-Shannon divergence between predicted distributions, used for nearest-neighbor retrieval of points with a similar geometric setting.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 (ImageNet-pretrained) + FPN + MLP implicit decoder; Audio-CNN for sound (trained on collision replay labels)
setting.training_data: Self-collected random walks in Habitat: 10x500 steps in each of 360 Gibson scenes (1.8M frames, filtered to 800K); Matterport3D with SoundSpaces for the sound experiment
setting.observation: Monocular RGB (256x256) for remote prediction, plus projected depth of query points; 32x32 RGB or binaural spectrogram for egocentric prediction
setting.action_space: Low-level: forward 25cm, turn +/-10° (+/-45° mean for egocentric data), turn around 180°, with LoCoBot-derived actuation noise
setting.privileged: none at test time (the projected depth of query points is computed from the camera pose); training uses simulator collision signals and, for the baselines, GT floorplans

numbers.extra: trained on noisy random walks with collision replay; distances in meters, delta=0.25m

results: Classification over collision-time distributions beats L1/L2 regression on distance-function MAE (0.11 vs 0.13/0.14 with angle conditioning). With noise-free walks it approaches the fully supervised floorplan encoder (MAE 0.10 vs 0.08) and the analytic depthmap projection (0.09). In the egocentric setting it beats regression (MAE 0.58 vs 0.96) and LFC (F1 0.66 vs 0.62 at k=8), and echolocation outperforms 32x32 images (MAE 0.58 vs 0.64).
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation with a random-walk policy and no real-robot experiments.
Floorplan IoU stays well below the supervised baseline (0.47-0.54 vs 0.66), and predictions are capped at a 10-step horizon.
Labels depend on intended egomotion, so actuation noise corrupts them; wall-vs-corner discrimination is weak (AUROC 0.55).
